Hope youre well. Thanks,
Jamie

Monica - quick note on policy: we allow one-off short extensions for active pilots but we escalate when we see concurrent extension requests that appear coordinated across multiple orgs or when account email domains differ from company domain. Please check for:
- overlapping IP addresses or simultaneous sign-ups from same subnet
- same credit-card/payment attempt patterns across accounts
- identical usage fingerprints (same prompts, same large batch calls)

If Peregrine provides the CSV I can run a quick heuristic check. If youre seeing anything that looks scripted, flag for Marissa for approval or decline.

Ben
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Note: internal policy doc: https://redwood-internal/ops/credits-policy

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial extension request for three teams

Following up with the CSV from Peregrine (attached). I ran a surface inspection and saw:
- Eight accounts across the three teams with overlapping creation timestamps on 2028-04-02 and 2028-04-03.
- Two accounts attempted payment authorization on the same card number (masked).
- High-volume parallel token usage at 03:00 UTC on multiple days (likely automated tests).

Im attaching the usage export and a screenshot of the payment attempts.

Quick ask: if this looks like coordinated multi-account testing, do we block further extensions and ask for centralized PO/seat-based trial? If its clean, I can grant the one-week extension.

Thanks,
Monica

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial extension request for three teams

Thanks for the summary and the artifacts. I reviewed the CSV and the masked payment patterns — this looks like coordinated parallel sign-ups more than independent team evaluations. Our risk tolerance for multi-account trial extensions is low because its frequently correlated with credit-stacking and scripted evaluation.

Decision: Decline blanket multi-account extension. Offer a targeted remediation path:
- Approve a single short extension for the canonical pilot account (one per company) while procurement completes PO (7 days max).
- Require Peregrine to consolidate the other test accounts under a single seat-based pilot or provide a signed letter from procurement confirming intent and timeline.
- Ask Peregrine to provide the HubSpot deal ID and a billing contact (we already have one copied).

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
---
Related internal note: escalate to security review if new sign-ups continue after the outreach.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Patel <jamie@peregrine-systems.com>
Cc: Peregrine Systems Billing <billing@peregrine-systems.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial extension request for three teams

Hi Jamie,

Thanks for the quick turn-around on the usage report. We reviewed the activity and payment artifacts and, to protect both sides, we cant approve simultaneous extensions for all accounts. However, we can do the following:

1) Immediate one-week extension for one canonical pilot account so your engineering team can finish the evaluation (I need the specific account ID you want extended).
2) For the other accounts, please consolidate them under one centralized pilot or confirm procurement timeline and provide a HubSpot deal ID so we can whitelist once a PO is in place.

If youd like, we can also schedule a 30-minute call today with Ben to walk through seat-based pricing and procurement next steps. If we see additional suspicious sign-up activity after this, well pause trial credit issuance and hand the case over to security for a deeper fraud check.

Appreciate your understanding — once you send the canonical account ID Ill apply the extension.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (650) 555-0198
